new_roles.title: Director of Operations - Hybrid
new_roles.description:
Director of Operations - Hybrid

**Role Overview:**

We are seeking a high-caliber, transformative **Director of Operations** to lead, scale, and optimize our operations. In this role, you will serve as a strategic leader responsible for driving operational excellence, customer advocacy, and regulatory integrity across a multi-faceted organization.

You will move beyond routine contact center management to steer a dynamic organization comprised of specialized internal operational teams—covering strategic readiness, advanced customer advocacy, and complex fraud/escalation management—alongside large-scale BPO vendor partners managing ~200+ frontline agents.

You bring a blend of strategic vision, process optimization discipline, vendor governance, and high-impact people leadership required to elevate operational standards and deliver best-in-class customer experiences.

**You have a proven track record of:**

* **Large-Scale Operations Leadership**: Successfully leading multi-site contact center operations combining internal teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners of 200+ headcount.
* **Operational Transformation**: Transforming reactive service centers into proactive, quality-focused customer advocacy hubs through structured process engineering.
* **Escalation & Fraud Management**: Effectively mitigating enterprise risk through robust Tier 2 & 3 complaint handling, fraud prevention protocols, and regulatory adherence.
* **Vendor Operations Governance**: Driving rigorous SLA performance, cost efficiency, and quality alignment across third-party BPO vendor organizations.

**What you’ll do:**

The Director of Operations maintains end-to-end accountability for operational strategy, performance delivery, vendor oversight, and organizational readiness.

* **Leadership Reach**: Direct oversight of Department Managers, Unit Managers (UMs), and Vendor Managers (VMs) across internal and external business units.
* **Core Internal Operations**:
 + **Strategic Operations:** Driving CX quality call listening, 1:1 and group coaching/training, operations readiness, and training materials maintenance.
 + **Customer Advocacy:** Overseeing high-touch inbound customer service, task execution, complex account resolution, and U.S. transfer handling.
 + **Escalations and Fraud**: Leading high-severity escalated problem solving, fraud operations, customer complaint research and resolution, and escalation follow-ups.
* **Core External Operations:**
 + Governance and SLA performance tracking for primary vendor partners overseeing a network of ~200+ non-associate vendor agents performing inbound calls and funding workflows.

**Key Focus Areas:**

* Reimagine end to end Operations in this era of AI
* Strategic Leadership & Governance to formulate and execute long-term operational strategies and partner cross functionally
* Partner cross-functionally with Product, Business Analysis, and Process teams to establish and update processes, policies, procedures, and standards
* Define operational KPIs, quality targets, and SLA metrics to ensure consistent service delivery, funding accuracy, and customer satisfaction
* Direct vendor management leads to oversee third-party partners, ensuring ~200+ vendor agents adhere to operational guidelines and productivity benchmarks
* Risk, Fraud, & Complaint Resolution spanning complex problem solving and root-cause analysis
* Ensure business readiness for product launches, process updates, and technology enhancements across all operational sub-functions
* Mentor, develop, and inspire a multi-layered leadership team, cultivating a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and high performance.
* Optimize talent allocation and capacity planning across teams to handle volume fluctuations dynamically.

**Location:** Plano, TX - This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree or military experience
* At least 5 years of people leadership experience
* At least 5 years of process or project management experience
* At least 5 years of relationship management experience
* At least 5 years of experience delivering transformational initiatives

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* PMP, Lean, Agile, or Six Sigma certification
* At least 3 years of operations people leadership experience
* At least 7 years of people leadership experience

**At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization, or offer any immigration related support for this position (e.g. H1B, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, TN, E-3, and O-1, or any other forms of work authorization that require immigration support from an employer)**

The minimum and maximum full-time annual salaries for this role are listed below, by location. Please note that this salary information is solely for candidates hired to perform work within one of these locations, and refers to the amount Capital One is willing to pay at the time of this posting. Salaries for part-time roles will be prorated based upon the agreed upon number of hours to be regularly worked.

Plano, TX: $173,000 - $197,400 for Director, Operations

Candidates hired to work in other locations will be subject to the pay range associated with that location, and the actual annualized salary amount offered to any candidate at the time of hire will be reflected solely in the candidate’s offer letter.

This role is also eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). Incentives could be discretionary or non discretionary depending on the plan.

Capital One offers a comprehensive, competitive, and inclusive set of health, financial and other benefits that support your total well-being. Learn more at the Capital One Careers website. Eligibility varies based on full or part-time status, exempt or non-exempt status, and management level.

This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.No agencies please. Capital One is an equal opportunity employer (EOE, including disability/vet) committed to non-discrimination in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Capital One promotes a drug-free workplace. Capital One will consider for employment qualified applicants with a criminal history in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable laws regarding criminal background inquiries, including, to the extent applicable, Article 23-A of the New York Correction Law; San Francisco, California Police Code Article 49, Sections 4901-4920; New York City’s Fair Chance Act; Philadelphia’s Fair Criminal Records Screening Act; and other applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations regarding criminal background inquiries.

If you have visited our website in search of information on employment opportunities or to apply for a position, and you require an accommodation, please contact Capital One Recruiting at 1-800-304-9102 or via email at RecruitingAccommodation@capitalone.com. All information you provide will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent required to provide needed reasonable accommodations.

For technical support or questions about Capital One's recruiting process, please send an email to Careers@capitalone.com

identity_held_roles.title: Head of Operational Excellence
identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

**Job Description**

The Head of Operational Excellence will lead operational excellence across Shield AI’s Group 3 UAV manufacturing in Frisco, TX (V-BAT) and Group 5 UAV manufacturing in Seattle, WA (X-BAT). Based in Frisco, this leader will create, deploy, and actively manage manufacturing KPIs and performance systems across both sites, embedding operating rhythms that improve accountability, visibility, and results. 
 
You will be responsible for instilling a culture of execution excellence, embedding structured problem-solving practices, and delivering measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, and productivity. This includes leading the development and governance of operational standards—such as visual management, 5S, and root cause analysis—while owning the manufacturing budget cycle, business rhythm, and executive reporting interface across both locations. This role partners with engineering, production, quality, and business functions to execute high-priority improvement initiatives, support V-BAT production, and establish operational excellence as X-BAT progresses through prototype and into rate production.

**Do you have the expertise and leadership to embed excellence into the fabric of autonomous defense manufacturing?**

### **What You'll Do:**

* Create, deploy, and actively manage consistent manufacturing KPIs and performance dashboards across both sites to drive visibility and accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.

* Define, train, deploy, and continually improve operational standards across V-BAT manufacturing in Frisco and X-BAT manufacturing in Seattle, including 5S, root cause analysis, and visual management.

* Develop and institutionalize the manufacturing budget process across both sites, including forecasting, controls, and performance tracking.

* Set financial targets in collaboration with operations and finance teams and drive adherence to budget and cost goals.

* Lead high-impact cross-functional improvement initiatives across both sites to improve quality, delivery, efficiency, productivity, and cost performance.

* Prepare and coordinate senior and executive-level reporting packages for Manufacturing leadership reviews.

* Partner with production, quality, and engineering teams to deploy Lean and continuous improvement practices, adapting execution to the needs of established production and prototype-to-rate manufacturing.

* Own business office functions for Manufacturing across both sites, including goal tracking, KPI dashboards, and process governance.

* Coach and train teams and leaders across both sites to elevate operational discipline, share effective practices, and sustain improvements.

### **Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or related field.

* Experience leading operational excellence, Lean, or business office programs within a manufacturing environment, with the ability to lead improvement across multiple sites.

* Demonstrated ability to design, roll out, and sustain structured operational standards and improvement systems.

* Strong background in budgeting, reporting, and performance management at a senior level.

* Excellent communication skills and experience preparing executive-level summaries and presentations.

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree or formal Lean Six Sigma certification.

* Experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware manufacturing environments.

* Proficiency with digital tools for KPI visualization, reporting automation, and business process tracking.

* Track record of influencing change across large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations and multiple sites.

$173,760 - $260,640 a year

Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

existing_roles.title: Director, External Quality Management
existing_roles.description:
**Description:**

The Director, Quality – External Manufacturing leads the External Quality team responsible for quality oversight of Amneal's network of 50+ external manufacturers, including contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), contract packagers, contract testing laboratories, and API/critical material suppliers across oral solid dose, injectables, and complex products. The role ensures that products manufactured or tested externally meet Amneal's quality standards, approved regulatory filings, and applicable cGMP requirements, and that Amneal's Quality Unit retains full accountability for outsourced operations. Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Quality, the Director leads a team of External Quality Managers and QA Leads, each accountable for a defined set of partners / activities, and works closely with Supply Chain, Procurement, Research & Development, and Regulatory Affairs.

**Essential Functions:**

* External Quality Leadership & Network Oversight - Lead quality oversight of 50+ external manufacturers, contract laboratories, and business partners. Establish a risk-based oversight model that tiers partners by product criticality, dosage form, regulatory history, and performance, and sets audit frequency, on-site presence, and review depth accordingly. Serve as the senior Quality decisionmaker for external manufacturing issues, product impact assessments, and escalations. Represent External Quality in management review and Quality Council forums.
* People Leadership - Lead, coach, and develop a team of External Quality Managers and QA Leads; assign partner portfolios and balance workload across 50+ sites. Build team capability in auditing, investigation review, risk assessment, and regulatory requirements. Develop and maintain SOPs, tools, and standard work for external quality oversight. Foster a culture of quality ownership, independent challenge, transparency, and continuous improvement.
* Quality Agreements & Partner Qualification – Own the authoring, negotiation, approval, and periodic review of Quality Agreements. Lead quality due diligence, qualification, and approval of new partners; maintain the Approved Supplier List. Define and execute the CMO and contract laboratory audit program; ensure audit observations are tracked to effective closure. Lead quality disqualification and exit decisions for persistently non-compliant partners.
* Batch Disposition & Product Quality - Ensure timely, compliant review and disposition of externally manufactured batches against approved specifications and registered processes. Oversee review of executed batch records, CoAs, and release testing performed at contract laboratories. Ensure Annual Product Reviews incorporate complete and accurate CMO data and drive actions from trends. Oversee stability program commitments, OOS/OOT trending, and product quality complaints for externally manufactured products.
* Deviations, Investigations & CAPA - Ensure deviations, OOS/OOT results, and complaints at partner sites are investigated thoroughly and in a timely manner. Challenge root cause analyses for scientific rigor and identification of systemic contributors. Approve CAPAs and verify effectiveness; identify recurring issues across partners and drive network-wide preventive actions. Lead quality assessments for field alerts, recalls, and market actions involving external products.
Change Control & Regulatory Alignment - Govern partner-initiated and Amneal-initiated changes through change control, including product impact and regulatory reportability assessments. Partner with Regulatory Affairs to ensure changes are filed appropriately (CBE-0, CBE-30, PAS, annual report) and that partner operations remain aligned with approved ANDAs/NDAs. Provide quality oversight of technology transfers, site transfers, process validation, and new product launches at external sites.  

This position requires 30-40% travel both domestic and international.

  

**Education:**

* Bachelor's Degree (BA/BS) Chemistry, biology, Pharmacy, engineering or other technical fields - Required
Master's degree (MS/MA) Chemistry, biology, Pharmacy, engineering or other technical fields - Preferred  

**Experience:**

* 15 years or more in QA, QC, Compliance in pharmaceutical manufacturing company.
* 5 years or more in External / CMO quality oversight.
Must have experience managing others.  

**Specialized Knowledge:**

* Demonstrated quality oversight of a large, multi-site CMO network across dosage forms (oral solids, sterile injectables, and/or complex generics).
* Expert knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210/211, 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP, ICH Q7/Q9/Q10, and FDA expectations for Quality Agreements and outsourced manufacturing.
* Experience hosting or supporting FDA inspections and leading 483 / Warning Letter remediation.
Strong background in investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA, and change control.  

The salary range for this position ranges from $205,000 - $236,000 per year. In addition, Amneal offers a short-term incentive opportunity, such as a bonus or performance-based award as well as a long-term incentive award, such as restricted stock units, with this position within the first 12 months. Amneal ranges reflect the Company’s good faith estimate of what Amneal reasonably believes that it will pay for said position at the time of the posting. Individual compensation will ultimately be determined based on a variety of relevant factors, including but not limited to, qualifications, experience, geographic location and other relevant skills.
  
  
At the heart of our Total Rewards commitment is a comprehensive, flexible and competitive benefits program for eligible positions that enables you to choose the plans and coverage that meet your personal needs. This includes above-market, diverse and robust health and insurance benefits to meet the varied needs of our employees as well as a significant 401(k) matching contribution to help our employees save for retirement. We also promote employee well-being with programs that help you enjoy your career alongside life’s many other commitments and opportunities.

  

Amneal is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process or to participate in any part of the hiring process, please contact us at accommodations@amneal.com . Requests will be handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable laws.

existing_roles.title: Director, Enterprise Quality & Assurance
existing_roles.description:
Requisition ID # 175673
  
  
**Job Category:** Compliance / Risk / Quality Assurance
  
**Job Level:** Director/Chief
  
**Business Unit:** Gen Counsel, Ethics, Risk & Compliance
  
**Work Type:** Hybrid
  
**Job Location:** Oakland
  
  
Position Summary
  
The Director of Enterprise Quality & Assurance will establish and lead the Enterprise Quality Management function under the Enterprise Risk & Compliance organization, providing an enterprise-wide framework to strengthen quality, promote consistent execution, and drive continuous improvement to PG&E’s Layers of Defense framework. Accountable for applying risk-informed assurance activities to increase confidence that operational processes and controls are effective and deliver intended safety, quality, compliance, and business outcomes. Plans, organizes, and directs assurance and quality management activities, leading staff and partnering with functional area coworkers to support PG&E’s collective success.
  
  
Reporting Relationship
  
This position reports to the Senior Director, Enterprise Assurance and will lead a team of 4 quality assurance professionals, both full-time employees and contractors. The Director will build the team as needed.
  
  
Job Responsibilities Defines enterprise-wide governance, standards, and performance measures to promote consistent execution, strengthen quality, and drive continuous improvement in partnership with functional leaders. Leads risk-informed assurance activities to increase confidence in operational process performance and risk management, with an initial focus on the Power Generation line of business. The Director will partner with asset, process, and risk owners to assess mitigation effectiveness and support executive-level communications. Applies a standardized, end-to-end work system framework to increase confidence in the performance of operational processes and controls that are designed and operating to manage risk and deliver intended safety, quality, compliance, and business outcomes. Serving as a trusted partner, leads assurance activities for PG&E’s operational processes and risks, including risk-related commitments, mitigation plans, and the use of risk models to inform work planning and operational decisions Partners with Internal Audit, Compliance, and Functional Area partners to strengthen PG&E’s Layers of Defense activities. Leads cross-functional teams to advance quality and process improvements, partnering with operational owners to implement corrective actions and applying follow-up assurance to assess their effectiveness Provides expert insight on operational risk, process performance, and quality management, translating assurance results into actionable recommendations for leaders and process owners. Produces reports and presentations that effectively communicate assurance findings, operational risk positions, quality trends, and improvement priorities, leveraging appropriate Lean tools and existing governance processes to support enhancing PG&E’s layers of defense framework.
  
  
Leadership Qualities
  
PG&E expects its leaders to conduct themselves with the highest ethics and integrity and to embody specific leadership qualities.
  
  
Strategic Mindset Seeing ahead to future possibilities and translating them into breakthrough strategies. Operating effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is not clear.
  
A Leader in the Community and Industry Effectively building formal and informal relationship networks inside and outside the organization. Anticipating and balancing the needs of multiple stakeholders.
  
Demonstrates Safety Leadership A safety champion in words and deeds with respect to both employee and public safety. Maintaining an environment of open dialog and free of retaliation.
  
Influences and Inspires Using various- communications that convey a clear understanding of the needs of different audiences. Maneuvering comfortably through complex policy, process, and people-related dynamics.
  
Optimizes Team Performance Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals. Creating a climate where people are developed and motivated to do their best to help the organization.
  
Fiscally Responsible Interpreting and applying understanding of key financial indicators to make better business decisions. Planning and prioritizing work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
  
Leads Ethically and in a Compliant Manner Sponsoring and sustaining a high integrity speak-up corporate culture which prioritizes ethics, safety and compliance. Building on necessary level of industry, company and subject-matter expertise, including laws and regulations.
  
Provides a High Level of Customer Service Building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions.
  
  
Background Qualifications
  
Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or job-related discipline or equivalent experience 10 years of successful professional experience with utility operations management Proven track record of successful leadership experience, leading and developing strong teams
  
  
Desired Master’s Degree in Business, Finance or job-related discipline or equivalent experience Proven experience with Quality Management Systems Operational experience with Electric Operations, Gas Operations, Power Generation, Diablo Canyon Excellent communication skills and attitude necessary to establish and maintain positive working relationships with all management and personnel. Strong analytical and risk assessment skills
  
  
Compensation
  
PG&E is providing the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might pay for this position at the time of the job posting. This compensation range is specific to the locality of the job. The actual salary paid to an individual will be based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, geographic location, and internal equity.
  
  
We estimate the successful candidate hired into this role will be placed within the reasonable compensation range of $193K to $277K . The decision will be made on a case-by-case basis. This leadership role is also eligible for an annual Short Term Incentive Plan (STIP) award, as well as the Long Term Incentive Plan (LTIP) grant.

existing_roles.title: Director of Quality Food Safety Business Partner
existing_roles.description:
At WK Kellogg Co, we exist to create joy and connection to inspire Gr-r-reat days. We believe that doing good is always good for business and we have stood for this since Kellogg Company was founded more than 120 years ago. We are passionate about doing our part to make nutritious foods, create social connectivity and respect natural resources. Together, these actions create positive progress for people and the planet – today and for years to come. We have big plans for how we are going to accomplish this, and we would love for you to join us in this effort.
  
  
The Director of Quality Food Safety (QFS) Business Partner – External Plant Network provides active leadership and sets priorities for quality, food safety and sanitation programs for the WK Kellogg Co RTEC External Network. Directs and coordinates plant quality, food safety, and sanitation personnel that enable the effective execution of innovation, policies, and standards through the delivery of tools, technical competency and capability building across all External Network plants, Co-Mans Co-Packers. Enables delivery of Business growth plans.
  
  
Ensures the investigation, root cause analysis, and corrective actions for serious and escalated issues. Responsible for functional development of direct reports.
  
  
Is a member of WK Kellogg Co QFS Leadership team.
  
  
**Dimensions:**  

* Manages travel budget
* Manages 4 Direct reports
* Ensures KIWS (Kellogg Integrated Work Systems) as the way of working

existing_roles.title: Director, United States Operations Quality Audits & Inspections
existing_roles.description:
Facility: Quality

Location:
Plainsboro, NJ, US

**About the Department**

  

The Clinical, Medical and Regulatory (CMR) department at Novo Nordisk is one of the most diverse and collaborative groups within the organization. From healthcare provider interactions and developing and implementing regulatory strategies with the FDA to providing medical education and collecting data to support efficacy and new product development, CMR is involved. The one thing that keeps us all marching to the same beat is our patient centered focus. At Novo Nordisk, you will help patients around the world. As their needs evolve, so does our challenge to find better and more innovative ways to improve their quality of life. We’re changing lives for a living. Are you ready to make a difference?

  

**The Position**

Lead independent, risk-based quality audits and inspection readiness across the approved USO Quality (USOQ) domain. Develop and execute the audit and self-inspection strategy to assess compliance, control effectiveness and risks to patient safety, product quality and data integrity across applicable current GxPs [Good Clinical (GCP), Pharmacovigilance (GPV), Distribution (GDP) and Manufacturing (GMP)] practices]. Maintain an objective view of business and Quality activities, including outsourced activities within scope. Lead sustained audit and inspection readiness and act as the designated local health authority inspection point of contact and inspection lead for the USOQ domain, coordinating with Regulatory Affairs, Global Quality, Patient Safety and accountable business leaders. Ensure readiness gaps and regulatory commitments are visible, owned, and escalated. Provide independent assurance over external-party quality controls through risk-based audits & remediation plans.

  

**Relationships**

Position reports to the Head of USO Quality. The sponsor approves the audit charter and risk-based plan, reviews resource adequacy, receives unfiltered findings and has formal input into the Director’s appointment, removal and performance assessment. The Director has direct access to the sponsor to escalate interference, disputed findings, scope restrictions and unresolved material risks. Interface with multiple Novo accountable business leaders, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, Safety, global Quality Audit and Global Clinical Compliance. External relationships include health authorities, clinical trial sites, external auditors and relevant vendors and partners. Coordinate USOQ inspection communications through approved authority channels without displacing global, legal-entity, Regulatory or Safety accountabilities. This role manages the independent audit and inspection department, with multiple experienced quality representatives assigned to diverse quality functions and includes auditor competence, inspection leadership, workload, budget and continuity.

  

**Essential Functions**

* Direct Independent Audits and Self-Inspection Program & Staff
* Maintain the USOQ audit charter, audit universe and risk-based audit and self-inspection strategy. Define scope, frequency, methods, auditor qualifications and escalation criteria across business functions, Quality verticals and relevant external parties. Secure approval of audit plans and material changes, ensure authorized access to personnel, sites, systems and records and align with global audit programs to prevent duplication and coverage gaps
* Lead the annual audit & self-inspection program, including routine, risk-triggered and for-cause reviews. Assign qualified, independent auditors; oversee evidence-based assessments of control design, effectiveness, data integrity and external-party controls. Ensure consistent finding classification, clear communication and timely reporting. Manage budget and staffing, document plan deviations and escalate material coverage or resource gaps
* Inspection Readiness and Health Authority Leadership
* Lead inspection readiness with business and Quality leaders through assessments, mock inspections, playbooks, document-retrieval exercises, SME preparation and trained deputies. Define inspection-team roles, front- and back-room responsibilities, request tracking and escalation. Coordinate USOQ administrative support while leading readiness coordination and independent challenge. Business and process owners retain responsibility for compliant operations, source records and readiness evidence
* Serve as the designated local health authority inspection contact and lead within approved USOQ scope, including FDA and other formally assigned authorities. Coordinate inspection logistics, meetings, interviews, requests and communications with Regulatory Affairs, global functions and accountable SMEs. Lead observation triage, response coordination and commitment tracking. Secure authorized approvals for submissions, commitments and risk acceptance; retain established company signatory, Regulatory and Safety reporting authorities
* Finding Ownership and Remediation Oversight
* Ensure all audit, self-inspection and inspection findings have accountable business or process owners, action owners, deadlines and escalation routes. Business leaders assign ownership and resources; finding owners investigate root causes, develop and implement CAPA and demonstrate effectiveness. Quality owns findings within its processes. Challenge inadequate responses and escalate unassigned, overdue, repeat or high-risk findings to the Head of USOQ and Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor, as appropriate. Honor health authority deadlines
* Independently assess audit and self-inspection responses and verify remediation effectiveness before closing findings under approved procedures. Require additional evidence or action where needed. For inspection observations, coordinate completion and effectiveness checks while preserving authorized response approvals and health authority closure decisions. Reviewers must not assess their own remediation; finding owners retain investigation, CAPA development and implementation
* Report audit themes, inspection readiness, overdue commitments and systemic risks to the Quality Council and relevant global forums. Escalate urgent risks immediately and independence concerns directly to the Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor
* Independence and Performance
* Protect audit objectivity through a documented charter, conflict disclosures, independent assignments and unfiltered reporting. Base conclusions on evidence, free from business or delivery pressures; escalate classification disputes through approved independent channels. Do not operate or approve controls the team audits; arrange independent review of its readiness and inspection-coordination activities. Track risk-based coverage, reporting and regulatory-response timeliness, readiness-gap closure, overdue and repeat findings, CAPA effectiveness and auditor competence. Do not incentivize low finding counts or guarantee inspection outcomes.
  

**Physical Requirements**

10-20% overnight travel required. This position (in-office) is located in Plainsboro, NJ.

  

**Development Of People**

Supervisory. Ensure that reporting personnel have individual development plans (IDP), with annual goals and measurements that are consistent with the priorities of the business and that interim reviews are held so that their work is focused on those priorities and they understand their level of accountability for results and the measurement process. Ensure that the IDP forms include completed learning and aspiration plans and are in place for all reporting personnel to enable the achievement of goals and capability to assume increased levels of responsibility. Manage the application and communication of all Novo Nordisk policies, procedures and Novo Nordisk Way.

  

**Qualifications**

* **Education level:** Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree preferred; advanced degree may substitute for 2 years of experience
* **Experience Level:** 10+ years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry, including at least 5 years in GxP Quality Assurance, Compliance, or related functions, and 5 years in people leadership or leading complex cross-functional quality initiatives. Demonstrated experience in commercial/affiliate quality, pharmacovigilance quality, regulatory inspections, and pharmaceutical Quality Management Systems (QMS). Broader GDP/GMP experience preferred.
* **Specific or technical job skills:** Deep expertise in GxP and FDA inspections; working knowledge of GPV/GDP/GMP/GCP and other requirements applicable to commercial & post-marketing operations. Demonstrated leadership of independent audits, self-inspection programs, inspection readiness and health authority inspections, including finding classification, root-cause/CAPA challenge and effectiveness verification. Ability to distinguish inspection coordination from business execution and authorized regulatory commitments  
  The base compensation range for this position is $187,100K to $327,000K. Base compensation is determined based on a number of factors. This position is also eligible for a company bonus based on individual and company performance. Novo Nordisk offers long-term incentive compensation and or company vehicles depending on the position's level or other company factors.

Employees are also eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs including medical, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; disability insurance; 401(k) savings plan; flexible spending accounts; employee assistance program; tuition reimbursement program; and voluntary benefits such as group legal, critical illness, identity theft protection, pet insurance and auto/home insurance. The Company also offers time off pursuant to its sick time policy, flex-able vacation policy, and parental leave policy.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

  

At Novo Nordisk, we're not chasing quick fixes – we're creating lasting change for long-term health. For over 100 years, we've been driven by a single purpose: to defeat serious chronic diseases and help millions of people live healthier lives. This dedication fuels our constant curiosity and inspires us to push the boundaries of what's possible in healthcare. We embrace diverse perspectives, seek out bold ideas, and build partnerships rooted in shared purpose. Together, we're making healthcare more accessible, treating and defeating diseases, and pioneering solutions that create change spanning generations. When you join us, you become part of something bigger – a legacy of impact that reaches far beyond today.

  

Novo Nordisk is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by local, state or federal laws, rules or regulations.

existing_roles.description:
Job Description
  
  
Position Overview
  
  
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
  
Global Quality Management Systems
  
  
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
  
  
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
  
  
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
  
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
  
  

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
  
  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
  
  

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:**  
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
  
  
**Preferred Skills:**  
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.

* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.

**Lead Strategy. Drive Performance. Shape the Future.**

KSP Group, Inc/Jensen Metal Products is seeking a hands-on manufacturing leader to drive operational excellence, strengthen accountability, improve execution, and build scalable operating systems across our manufacturing businesses. This is not a corporate executive role designed to lead from a conference room.

We are looking for a proven change agent who is equally comfortable reviewing financial results, leading daily operational reviews, solving production challenges on the shop floor, and developing frontline leaders.

This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.

**About KSP Group**

KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies

* **Jensen Metal Products** – Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
* **Jensen Powder Finishers** – Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI)
* **Jensen Castings** – Manufacturer of premium GFRC concrete fire features (Richland Center, WI)
* **Real Flame** – A leading designer and manufacturer of fireplaces, fire tables, and outdoor living products sold through major retailers across North America (Union Grove, WI)

Together, our companies are built on innovation, craftsmanship, customer partnerships, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a visible impact, influence company strategy, and help shape the future of multiple growing businesses.

**What You'll Do**

Executive Strategic & Business Leadership

* Lead the development and execution of operational strategies that support long-term business objectives and growth initiatives
* Partner with executive leadership to establish priorities, allocate resources, and drive enterprise-wide operational improvements
* Lead plant leadership teams in defining strategic direction, performance goals, and key operational initiatives
* Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, capacity expansion, and operational scalability

Financial & Operational Performance

* Own operational performance and P&L results across assigned manufacturing operations
* Develop departmental budgets, monitor spending, and ensure responsible management of operational resources
* Analyze manufacturing costs, labor efficiency, productivity metrics, and operating expenses to drive profitability
* Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership

Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives across fabrication, welding, machining, powder coating, assembly, engineering, and support functions
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, root cause problem solving, and waste reduction efforts
* Improve throughput, quality, safety, delivery performance, and overall operational efficiency
* Lead cross-functional projects focused on sustainable operational gains and measurable business results

Leadership & Culture

* Build, coach, and develop high-performing operational leadership teams
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement
* Promote employee engagement while creating a safe, quality-focused work environment

Requirements:

**What We're Looking For**

* Demonstrated success leading directly from the manufacturing floor, including personal involvement in:
* Production planning and scheduling
* Labor performance management
* Quality improvement initiatives
* Corrective action processes
* Maintenance and equipment planning
* Capital investment justification
* Safety and operational accountability
* Frontline leadership development
* Proven track record of transforming entrepreneurial manufacturing organizations into process-driven, scalable operations through both strategic leadership and active engagement with frontline teams
* Ability to establish accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy
* Strong understanding of fabrication, welding, machining, finishing, assembly, materials management, and manufacturing cost drivers

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or related field, preferred
* Multi-site manufacturing leadership experience
* Lean Six Sigma certification
* Experience within both contract manufacturing and consumer products environments
* ERP/MRP system experience

**Travel Requirements**

* Regular travel between KSP Group facilities, including Jensen Metal Products, Jensen Powder Finishers, Jensen Castings, and Real Flame locations
* Frequent presence on manufacturing floors to support leadership teams, operational reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Approximately 25-50% travel, primarily within Wisconsin and company operating locations
* Occasional overnight travel for customer visits, supplier meetings, strategic initiatives, and industry events

**About Us**

Jensen Metal Products is a metal fabrication business with over 100 years of experience serving the Midwest and surrounding regions with custom, quality sheet metal parts and assemblies. With a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, we produce a diverse portfolio of products, including our own line of fireplaces, which has been in production since 1970. We serve many types of businesses including the agricultural, retail, energy and healthcare fields. From engineering to packaging, our goal is to be a one-stop shop that exceeds our customers’ expectations for quality, delivery, great customer service and cost. At Jensen Metal Products we pride ourselves on having strong, long-lasting relationships with our employees and customers. We welcome you to join our team!

* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options (HDHP and copay), FSA benefits, and the ability to use your existing HSA

* Company-sponsored team events and outings that foster connection and celebrate team success

Jensen Metal Products does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

**Recruiting Agencies**

We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.
  
  
Position Brand Description
  
How would you like a career where you get to apply your best technical and analytical skills to bring complex, high-potency biologic medicines to patients? We are seeking a scientific leader on our Parenteral Product Network Technical Services/Manufacturing Science (TS/MS) team to drive the commercialization of lyophilized drug products, with a focus on antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), and to provide technical support for commercial lyophilized product manufacturing.
  
In this role, you are critical to the success of Lilly’s oncology and biologics portfolio. As a Global Product Steward and lyophilization process expert, you will hold technical ownership of assigned lyophilized ADC and other parenteral products from late-stage development through the commercial lifecycle, serving as the technical link between Product Development and our commercial manufacturing sites. You will ensure these products are successfully launched, reliably supplied, and technically well controlled across internal and external sites.
  
  
Responsibilities

* Advance lyophilization technology in commercial manufacturing
* Maintain the product technical knowledge base and lifecycle strategy, including process history, critical material and supplier knowledge, a product technical risk register, and a roadmap for yield, robustness, capacity, and site-network improvements.
* Collaborate with product development and manufacturing site for technology transfer, scale-up, process performance qualification/validation, and comparability activities (including lyophilization cycle transfer between freeze-dryers of differing scale and design) to support commercial launch readiness.
* Escalate significant technical, quality, safety, compliance, and supply risks to TS/MS management in a timely manner, providing risk assessments, impact to patients and supply, and recommended mitigation plans.
* Own the commercial control strategy for lyophilization critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, and maintain process understanding through continued process verification, stability and batch trending, and global product assessment.
* Partner with Product Development to ensure manufacturability of new ADC and lyophilized products, and to provide commercial manufacturing feedback that informs formulation, cycle design, specifications, container closure selection, and site selection.

* PhD degree with 5 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Master’s degree with 10 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Bachelor’s degree with 15 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing.
* Hands-on experience with lyophilization development or manufacturing (e.g., formulation and cycle development, scale-up, tech transfer, or commercial cycle support).
* Working knowledge of protein-based and ADC drug product formulation and aseptic fill/finish processes.
* Experience supporting GMP commercial manufacturing, including technology transfer, process validation, and/or deviation investigation and resolution.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B or TN status) for this employment position.

* Background in lyophilized product development, including formulation and excipient selection, freeze-drying cycle design, and thermal characterization, and cycle scale-up.

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world's transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people's quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

**Job Summary**

Kairos Power is seeking an experienced senior engineering leader to serve as Director, Balance of Plant (Power Generation System & Turbine Island), to provide strategic and technical leadership for multidisciplinary engineering teams. This role is responsible for the technical leadership, organizational capability, and execution of the engineering teams responsible for design and deployment for Structures, Systems, and Components that convert thermal energy to electricity and provide auxiliary plant functions necessary to support reliable and efficient plant operation. The ideal candidate combines broad power plant and thermal-fluid systems expertise with demonstrated success building engineering teams, working with external partners, and delivering complex, hardware systems from concept through commissioning and operation.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and technical leadership for the development and integration of balance-of-plant (BOP) Systems, such as the Heat Transport Systems interfacing with high-temperature steam Rankine cycles, Power Generation System (PGS), and auxiliary systems such as service water, treated water, and compressed air systems.
* Establish department technical direction and decision boundaries consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.
* Lead engineering delivery from conceptual sizing through detailed design, vendor package review, and commissioning support, owning design reviews and technical risk.

* Ensure engineering deliverables—including requirements, calculations, analyses, specifications, drawings, design reports, interface documents, and test plans—are technically sound and meet established quality and schedule requirements.

* Other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or equivalent
* 15+ years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving power generation, thermal-fluid systems, process systems, nuclear systems, or other complex industrial systems.
* 7+years of progressive engineering leadership experience managing engineering teams with multiple engineering disciplines.
* Experience managing engineering managers or technical leads with accountability for outcomes across multiple teams and work sites.
* Experience working with suppliers, OEMs, engineering contractors, or other external technical organizations.
* Experience leading technical development and qualification of major equipment through external suppliers or OEMs.
* Experience supporting construction, commissioning, startup, or operation of complex power generation or industrial facilities.
* Experience with integrated power plant systems, including modern high-temperature steam Rankine cycles and the interactions between heat transport, power conversion, auxiliary systems, and plant infrastructure.
* Strong systems thinking with the ability to identify and resolve technical issues that cross traditional engineering and organizational boundaries.
* Lead and support recruitment and staffing requirements of group.
* Proactive, organized, adaptable, and able to thrive in fast-paced, multi-tasked environments.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Knowledge of integrated power plant architecture, thermal-fluid systems, power generation systems, auxiliary systems, major plant equipment, and their interfaces, including familiarity with various steam generator technologies such as Heat Recovery Steam Generators and molten salt steam generators.
* Knowledge of equipment procurement, supplier engineering, manufacturing, testing, installation, commissioning, and lifecycle considerations associated with complex industrial systems.

* Skill in translating program objectives into engineering strategies, priorities, resource plans, and measurable commitments.

Catalent’s Greendale, Indiana site is a key part of the company’s Wellness business, serving as one of North America’s primary gummy development and manufacturing centers. The site specializes in the formulation and production of traditional gelatin gummies and 100% plant‑based pectin gummies for nutritional supplements and nutraceutical applications, supporting a wide range of consumer health products. With strong in‑house R&D, quality laboratories, and flexible manufacturing and packaging capabilities, the Greendale operation partners closely with customers to develop innovative, high‑quality, and consumer‑friendly gummy delivery formats across a variety of flavors, shapes, and functional ingredients, all produced under rigorous quality and food‑safety standards.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager, Quality Systems to join our team and lead the Quality and Compliance functions at the Catalent Greendale site. This role oversees a team of Quality Assurance Supervisors and Specialists responsible for operational quality, product sampling, testing, and release. The position ensures compliance with industry standards and regulations while driving continuous improvement across the Quality organization. The successful candidate will collaborate with cross‑functional teams to maintain product integrity and ensure the consistent delivery of high‑quality products to our customers.

Shift: Monday through Friday, 8:00AM - 5:00PM  
Location: Greendale, IN  
100% Onsite

* Lead a team of Quality Assurance Supervisors and Specialists responsible for operational quality, product sampling, testing, and product release.

The individual may be required to sit, stand, walk regularly, and occasionally lift up to 15 pounds; no lifting greater than 44.09 pounds without assistance. * Experience with investigation writing, including root cause analysis and report preparation for annual product reviews.

* Experience with electronic systems such as JDE, TrackWise, Electronic Document Management System, Learning Management System, Quality Management System, Veeva, Compliance Wire, and Stability Programs.
* Experience communicating with FDA inspectors or other regulatory agents and handling FDA 483 responses.
* Experience using artificial intelligence tools to improve quality systems.

* Tuition Reimbursement – support to complete or earn a new degree.

The Advanced Operations Technology (AOT) organization is seeking an experienced and visionary Senior Manager, Digital Factory, to lead the strategy, architecture, and implementation of digital manufacturing technologies across our solid rocket motor manufacturing enterprise. Graduate Degree with a minimum of 10 years of prior digital manufacturing, OT/IIoT systems, manufacturing technology experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 16 years of prior digital manufacturing, OT/IIoT systems, manufacturing technology experience.

**Job Title:**

Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering (Burnet, TX)

**Job Description:**

**THE ROLE**

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering is responsible for leading manufacturing quality across two Entegris manufacturing sites in Texas and translating global quality standards and quality priorities into consistent site execution. This role provides multi-site leadership to reduce risk, strengthen process capability, improve customer satisfaction, and deliver measurable quality improvements across the two-site footprint.  
  
The Senior Manager partners with site Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Customer Quality, Product Quality and Quality Systems teams to embed quality ownership into daily operations. This leader is accountable for site quality performance, consistent implementation of quality standards, compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, and customer requirements, and the development of capable site quality teams. The role leads through site quality leaders and teams, establishes clear ownership and follow-through, and escalates risks and resource needs to North America quality leadership.

The hired individual will work on-site at our Burnet, TX location with some travel to our Decatur, TX location.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Translate global quality standards and quality priorities into coordinated execution plans for the two Texas sites, with clear owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
* Lead manufacturing quality across all two sites through site quality leaders and teams; clarify responsibilities, prioritize resources based on risk, and maintain regular on-site engagement.
* Ensure consistent implementation of global quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices; maintain audit readiness and timely closure of findings at each site.
* Partner with site Operations leaders to establish quality roadmaps, objectives, and common key performance indicators (KPIs); conduct routine cross-site reviews and drive recovery plans where performance falls short.
* Own quality improvement plans that reduce defects, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality (COPQ), customer complaints, and manufacturing escapes, with site-level accountability for results.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve process capability, product conformity, yield, and manufacturing performance through effective process controls and proactive risk management.
* Lead targeted continuous improvement and change implementation across the two sites; standardize effective practices and verify that improvements are sustained.
* Ensure timely containment, disciplined root cause analysis, corrective/preventive action, and effectiveness verification for significant quality issues; deploy lessons learned across all two sites.
* Ensure practical, sustained application of SPC, MSA, FMEA, control plans, APQP, PPAP, 8D, A3, and DMAIC methodologies, as applicable to site processes and customer requirements.
* Serve as the quality escalation leader for the two Texas sites; communicate risk, containment status, recovery plans, and decisions needed, and escalate significant issues to Quality leadership.
* Partner with Customer Quality and Product Quality teams to resolve customer issues through timely, evidence-based investigations, effective corrective actions, and proactive communication.
* Develop site quality leaders and teams through coaching, clear expectations, technical capability building, and succession planning; identify staffing and resource needs across the two sites.
* Foster shared quality ownership across functions, reinforce accountability for commitments, and promote collaboration and continuous improvement across the two sites.
* Travel requirements will be a minimum of 25%, including regular presence across the two Texas sites.

**WHAT WE SEEK**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related field required.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing quality, including leadership responsibility for quality teams and manufacturing quality outcomes.
* 5+ years of quality management experience, with demonstrated ability to lead through site leaders or cross-functional teams; multi-site leadership experience preferred.
* Demonstrated success implementing quality systems and delivering sustained improvements in manufacturing quality, process capability, and cost of poor quality.
* Ability to coordinate priorities, standardize practices, and maintain effective leadership presence across two manufacturing sites in Texas.
* Experience supporting customer and supplier quality requirements, audit readiness, and compliance with applicable regulatory and industry requirements.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence site leaders, resolve competing priorities, and communicate risks and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Demonstrated experience coaching quality leaders, developing technical capability, and building team depth and succession readiness across sites.
* Demonstrated ability to lead practical change, establish clear ownership, and sustain common quality practices in partnership with Operations and Engineering.
* Strong problem-solving, data analysis, and business acumen, with practical application of quality tools to prioritize risk, improve manufacturing processes, and deliver measurable results.

**WHY WORK AT ENTEGRIS?**  
Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future.  
  
Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.

**WHAT WE OFFER**  
Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals.

At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels included, respected, empowered and recognised.

**What You Can Expect**
-----------------------

The Director, NPI Execution, M&A Integration & Supplier Transfers leads strategic execution across new product introduction, acquired-business integration, and supplier/manufacturing transfer initiatives. This senior leader is accountable for ensuring products, processes, supply chains, and teams transition successfully from development, acquisition, or incumbent suppliers into stable, compliant, scalable operations.  
The role requires strong business judgment, deep supply-base knowledge, technical fluency, and the ability to lead complex programs in a regulated medical-device environment. The Director partners closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Finance, Manufacturing Engineering, and leadership to deliver continuity of supply, cost competitiveness, product quality, and growth objectives.  
  
Reports to: Senior Director Procurement (Cost Center - M&A)  
Direct reports: Integration Program leaders, supplier-transfer leaders, NPI project managers, supplier development personnel

**How You'll Create Impact**
----------------------------

1. NPI Execution and Operational Readiness  

* Lead the end-to-end operational execution of New Product Introduction programs, from design-transfer planning through commercialization and sustained production.
* Establish integrated NPI execution plans & Ensure alignment between product development timelines and operational deliverables, including design transfer, process characterization, validation, supplier readiness, and product availability.
* Drive structured phase-gate governance with external suppliers , program reviews, escalation mechanisms, and executive decision-making for high-priority launches.

  
2. M&A Operations Integration  

* Serve as the Procurement lead for M&A integrations.

* Lead Procurement part of integration governance, ensuring milestones, decisions, risks, and accountabilities are visible and managed at the appropriate leadership level.

  
3. Supplier Transfer and Supply-Base Optimization  

* Lead complex supplier-transfer programs, including strategic sourcing transitions, supplier exits, dual-source strategies, vertical-integration initiatives, and manufacturing footprint changes.
* Develop transfer strategies that balance continuity of supply, quality, technical feasibility, regulatory requirements, cost, capacity, and timing.
* Ensure supplier transfers are executed in accordance with applicable quality-system requirements, change-control processes, validation requirements, and regulatory commitments.
* Direct supplier selection, qualification, technical transfer, process validation, first-article activities, production ramp-up, and supplier performance monitoring.

  
4. People Leadership and Organizational Capability  

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of program, technical, supply-chain, and supplier-management professionals.
* Set clear goals, priorities, performance expectations, and development plans for direct reports.
* Build succession capability and strengthen organizational depth in NPI execution, technical operations, supplier transfer, and integration management.
* Foster cross-functional collaboration among teams with potentially competing objectives, timelines, and priorities.

Leadership  

* Builds high-performing teams and develops future leaders.
* Establishes clarity, accountability, and disciplined execution
* Leads through ambiguity, organizational change, and competing business priorities.

Business Acumen  

* Connects technical and operational decisions to financial, customer, and enterprise outcomes.
* Evaluates strategic tradeoffs with an enterprise-wide perspective.
* Identifies opportunities for value creation, risk reduction, and sustainable growth.

Technical and Procurement Expertise  

* Understands manufacturing processes, product industrialization, supplier capabilities, process controls, validation, and quality-system expectations.

Program Execution  

* Drives complex initiatives from strategy through implementation and stabilization.
* Uses effective governance, metrics, risk management, and escalation practices.
* Maintains focus on customer service, quality, compliance, delivery, and financial results.

Influence and Collaboration  

* Builds credibility with senior leaders, technical experts, plant leadership, suppliers, and all other stakeholders.
* Resolves conflict constructively and aligns diverse stakeholders behind common objectives.
* Communicates complex issues in a concise, actionable manner.

**Your Background**
-------------------

* Approximately 20 years of progressive experience in medical devices, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, or another highly regulated industry.
* Hands on experience & leadership experience in one or more of the following areas:
* New Product Introduction and product industrialization
* Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management
* Supplier Transfers or Manufacturing Transfers
