existing_roles.title: Director of Production - Grand Prix Plaza
existing_roles.description:
**Grand Prix Plaza, home of the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix,** is a world-class entertainment and event destination spanning approximately 39 acres in the heart of the Las Vegas Grand Prix circuit. The 300,000-square-foot facility features immersive Formula 1 attractions, premium hospitality experiences, event and meeting venues, retail, food and beverage offerings, and year-round activations that attract guests from across the globe. As both a daily operating entertainment venue and a critical component of one of the world's most recognized sporting events, Grand Prix Plaza requires a high-performing operational structure capable of delivering exceptional experiences while maintaining the highest standards of safety, service, and facility excellence.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**
=====================

The **Director of Production** serves as the leader responsible for all the experiences and production operations across Grand Prix Plaza. This position provides strategic leadership for Production, Guest Experience, Box Office, and Karting operations, ensuring all attractions, technical systems, guest interactions, and show elements consistently deliver a premium and memorable experience.

Working closely with the General Manager and cross-functional departments, the Director of Production drives operational strategy, financial performance, workforce development, guest satisfaction, and continuous innovation across the venue's immersive attractions and entertainment offerings. This role is responsible for ensuring all production and guest experience elements remain operationally ready to support daily business, private events, seasonal activations, and the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**
====================

* Develop and execute operational strategies that support organizational goals, business growth, and long-term venue objectives.
* Provides overall leadership and direction for Production, Guest Experience, Box Office, and Karting departments.
* Leads, develops, and mentors departmental leadership teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.
* Establishes operational standards, guest service expectations, performance metrics, and departmental goals to drive exceptional guest satisfaction and revenue performance.
* Oversees annual operating budgets, capital planning, labor strategies, and financial performance for all production and guest-facing departments.
* Directs the planning, integration, and execution of attraction enhancements, technical upgrades, new experiences, venue activations, and special events.
* Provides executive oversight of attraction reliability, show quality, technical systems, and operational readiness across all guest-facing experiences.
* Manages key vendor relationships, production partners, service providers, and equipment suppliers to ensure performance, quality, and financial objectives are achieved.
* Partners with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to support venue-wide initiatives, operational readiness, and organizational goals.
* Ensures compliance with all applicable safety standards, operational procedures, regulatory requirements, and risk management practices associated with attractions, entertainment, and guest operations.
* Other responsibilities as assigned

**QUALIFICATIONS**
==================

* 9+ years of progressive leadership experience within entertainment venues, attractions, theme parks, sports venues, immersive experiences, or hospitality operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading multi-disciplinary teams across production, guest experience, attractions, entertainment, box office, or related operational functions.
* Proven experience managing operating budgets, labor planning, capital expenditures, and departmental financial performance.
* Strong knowledge of attraction operations, live entertainment production, technical systems, guest experience management, and venue operations.
* Experience overseeing third-party vendors, production contractors, service providers, and strategic partnerships.
* Knowledge of OSHA requirements, risk management practices, life safety standards, and operational compliance requirements.
* Experience supporting large-scale events, attraction launches, venue activations, or public-facing entertainment operations.
* Strong business knowledge with the ability to analyze operational metrics, guest feedback, revenue performance, and financial reporting.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

**WORK SCHEDULE:**

* This is a full-time position that works a flexible schedule including weekdays, weekends, evenings, and holidays.

**SEASONAL & EVENT-BASED RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* This role includes a seasonal period during which responsibilities extend beyond standard operations. During load-in and load-out of the Grand Prix Plaza facility, race week activations, and other special projects, this position may support non-traditional functions that fall outside a routine. Flexibility, cross-functional collaboration, and adaptability are essential and required during these high-impact times.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**

* Physical ability to walk, stand, take stairs/elevators/escalators, and navigate the elements during the day and night
* May need to remain in a sitting or standing position for prolonged periods, and repeat motions that may include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers
* Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
* Ability to handle exposure to loud noises at live events, attractions, entertaining programs, and crowd
* Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at times.

**Other Duties:** Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

existing_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence
existing_roles.description:
Founded in 1967, ImageFIRST® is the largest and only national linen rental and laundry service specializing in the healthcare market. Acquired by private equity firm Calera Capital in 2018, ImageFIRST serves medical facilities nationwide providing linen, patient gowns, scrubs, and more while managing their clients’ linen inventory for cost management. As leaders in infection prevention, they currently own and operate the most HLAC-accredited facilities in the industry. With one of the highest customer retention rates in the industry – 97% – ImageFIRST is dedicated to improving patient satisfaction and making staff happy with our white glove service!

Check out our company page: https://www.imagefirst.com/company/

**Director, Operational Excellence - CAPEX**
============================================

**Location:** East Coast (Northeast Preferred)  
**Travel:** Approximately 50%

**Position Summary**
--------------------

ImageFIRST is seeking a strategic, hands-on **Director, Operational Excellence** to lead enterprise-wide engineering initiatives, capital project planning, and operational improvement efforts across our national network of healthcare laundry facilities.

This newly created leadership role will serve as a key partner to Operations and the Senior Leadership Team, driving long-term asset strategy, **capital investment planning**, engineering support, and operational sustainability. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing strategic initiatives, leading complex projects, and rolling up their sleeves to solve operational challenges in the field.

This role offers a unique opportunity to build foundational processes that will standardize engineering practices and strengthen operational performance across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital Planning & Strategic Investments**

* Identify, prioritize, and develop capital expenditure (Capex) opportunities across the network.
* Build financial justifications, ROI analyses, and business cases for capital investments.
* Present capital recommendations and project proposals to the Senior Leadership Team.
* Partner with Finance and Operations to align capital investments with business strategy and growth objectives.

### **Project Engineering Leadership**

* Lead enterprise engineering projects from concept through implementation.
* Provide technical leadership for facility upgrades, equipment installations, automation initiatives, and operational improvements.
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and with measurable business impact.

### **Engineering Support for Plant Operations**

* Serve as a technical resource for manufacturing and plant leadership across the ImageFIRST network.
* Provide engineering guidance and problem-solving support for facilities requiring operational or technical assistance.
* Partner with General Managers and Operations Leaders to resolve complex equipment and process challenges.

### **Operational Excellence & Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead cross-functional operational improvement initiatives that support network stabilization, sustainability, and long-term operational performance.
* Partner with Operations Leadership to identify opportunities for increased efficiency, standardization, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a trusted resource for high-impact operational projects across the business.

### **Safety Leadership**

* Champion a culture of safety across engineering and operational initiatives.
* Ensure engineering projects and equipment installations meet all applicable safety standards and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Environmental Health & Safety leadership to proactively reduce operational risk.

**Qualifications**
------------------

### **Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, industrial operations, engineering, or capital project management.
* Experience leading multi-site engineering or operational initiatives.
* Proven experience managing capital projects and developing ROI-driven business cases.
* Strong knowledge of asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and reliability.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders at all organizational levels.
* Strong financial acumen with experience presenting recommendations to executive leadership.
* Ability to travel approximately 50%.

### **Preferred**

* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing or industrial facilities.
* Plant management or operations leadership experience.
* Lean Manufacturing, TPM, Six Sigma, or Continuous Improvement experience.
* Military leadership experience is highly valued, particularly candidates who have transitioned into manufacturing, engineering, or operations leadership roles.
* Experience within healthcare services, industrial laundry, textiles, food manufacturing, consumer products, or other asset-intensive industries.

**Leadership Competencies**
---------------------------

* Strategic thinker with strong operational execution
* Results-oriented and highly accountable
* Excellent communication and executive presentation skills
* Strong analytical and financial decision-making capabilities
* Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence across functions
* Comfortable navigating ambiguity and leading enterprise-wide change
* Hands-on problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset

**Required Competencies:**

* Be Respectful: Value all we come in contact with
* Be Remarkable: Create a positive moment with every interaction
* Be Safe: Keep ourselves and those around us safe
* Be Honest: Be guided by truthfulness in all we do

**Benefits:**

* Weekly pay
* Medical, Dental, Vision
* Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
* 401k (match)
* Paid Time Off Package
* Paid Parental Leave
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Referral Program
* Great company culture
* Collaborative team environment

EOE / Drug-Free Workplace

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are fueled by the talent, passion, and diversity of our associates.

**Position Summary...**
-----------------------

**What you'll do...**
---------------------

The Director of Continuous Improvement leads monitoring, assurance, risk intelligence, control effectiveness, remediation, and transformation across Last Mile Delivery's Trust and Safety pillar focused on risk operations. This role identifies improvement opportunities, assesses whether risks and controls are effectively managed, determines root causes, and ensures corrective actions deliver sustainable results. The leader will evolve traditional quality assurance into a closed-loop assurance model that detects systemic issues, drives accountable remediation, and validates effectiveness. The role also leads operational resiliency through process redesign, business continuity, data-driven insights, tech automation —challenging how work is performed and designing scalable, sustainable solutions.
  
**About the team:**

Job Description
  
  
Position Overview
  
  
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
  
Global Quality Management Systems
  
  
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
  
  
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
  
  
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
  
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
  
  

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
  
  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
  
  

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:**  
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
  
  
**Preferred Skills:**  
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

protected_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources

Kairos Power is seeking an experienced senior engineering leader to serve as Director, Balance of Plant (Power Generation System & Turbine Island), to provide strategic and technical leadership for multidisciplinary engineering teams. This role is responsible for the technical leadership, organizational capability, and execution of the engineering teams responsible for design and deployment for Structures, Systems, and Components that convert thermal energy to electricity and provide auxiliary plant functions necessary to support reliable and efficient plant operation. The ideal candidate combines broad power plant and thermal-fluid systems expertise with demonstrated success building engineering teams, working with external partners, and delivering complex, hardware systems from concept through commissioning and operation.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and technical leadership for the development and integration of balance-of-plant (BOP) Systems, such as the Heat Transport Systems interfacing with high-temperature steam Rankine cycles, Power Generation System (PGS), and auxiliary systems such as service water, treated water, and compressed air systems.
* Establish department technical direction and decision boundaries consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.
* Lead engineering delivery from conceptual sizing through detailed design, vendor package review, and commissioning support, owning design reviews and technical risk.

* Ensure engineering deliverables—including requirements, calculations, analyses, specifications, drawings, design reports, interface documents, and test plans—are technically sound and meet established quality and schedule requirements.
* Oversee supplier technical execution, including supplier selection, bid evaluations, equipment specifications, design reviews, technical evaluations, qualification programs, factory acceptance testing, and resolution of supplier technical issues, to ensure supplier designs and deliverables meet Kairos Power requirements.
* Oversee evaluation of BOP design and supplier changes for impacts on system interfaces, plant performance, safety, and commissioning readiness, and ensure approved changes are incorporated into the controlled technical baseline.
* Build productive relationships with external organizations while maintaining clear accountability for Kairos Power technical requirements and engineering decisions.
* Translates company strategy into measurable organizational priorities and decision principles.
* Determine and communicate explicit scope, schedule, risk, and resource tradeoffs across the organization.
* Maintain accountability for organizational outcomes and the consequences of scope, schedule, risk, and resource decisions within delegated authority, including decisions delegated to others.

* Establish organizational technical direction and decision boundaries are established, consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.

* Build the organization and leadership pipeline required for current and future strategy, including recruitment, staffing, and leadership development.

* Other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving power generation, thermal-fluid systems, process systems, nuclear systems, or other complex industrial systems.
* 7+years of progressive engineering leadership experience managing engineering teams with multiple engineering disciplines.
* Experience managing engineering managers or technical leads with accountability for outcomes across multiple teams and work sites.
* Experience working with suppliers, OEMs, engineering contractors, or other external technical organizations.
* Experience leading technical development and qualification of major equipment through external suppliers or OEMs.
* Experience supporting construction, commissioning, startup, or operation of complex power generation or industrial facilities.

* Strong systems thinking with the ability to identify and resolve technical issues that cross traditional engineering and organizational boundaries.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Knowledge of integrated power plant architecture, thermal-fluid systems, power generation systems, auxiliary systems, major plant equipment, and their interfaces, including familiarity with various steam generator technologies such as Heat Recovery Steam Generators and molten salt steam generators.
* Knowledge of equipment procurement, supplier engineering, manufacturing, testing, installation, commissioning, and lifecycle considerations associated with complex industrial systems.

Catalent’s Greendale, Indiana site is a key part of the company’s Wellness business, serving as one of North America’s primary gummy development and manufacturing centers. **Job Title:**

Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering (Burnet, TX)

**Job Description:**

**THE ROLE**

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering is responsible for leading manufacturing quality across two Entegris manufacturing sites in Texas and translating global quality standards and quality priorities into consistent site execution. This role provides multi-site leadership to reduce risk, strengthen process capability, improve customer satisfaction, and deliver measurable quality improvements across the two-site footprint.  
  
The Senior Manager partners with site Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Customer Quality, Product Quality and Quality Systems teams to embed quality ownership into daily operations. This leader is accountable for site quality performance, consistent implementation of quality standards, compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, and customer requirements, and the development of capable site quality teams. The role leads through site quality leaders and teams, establishes clear ownership and follow-through, and escalates risks and resource needs to North America quality leadership.

The hired individual will work on-site at our Burnet, TX location with some travel to our Decatur, TX location.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Translate global quality standards and quality priorities into coordinated execution plans for the two Texas sites, with clear owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
* Lead manufacturing quality across all two sites through site quality leaders and teams; clarify responsibilities, prioritize resources based on risk, and maintain regular on-site engagement.
* Ensure consistent implementation of global quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices; maintain audit readiness and timely closure of findings at each site.
* Partner with site Operations leaders to establish quality roadmaps, objectives, and common key performance indicators (KPIs); conduct routine cross-site reviews and drive recovery plans where performance falls short.
* Own quality improvement plans that reduce defects, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality (COPQ), customer complaints, and manufacturing escapes, with site-level accountability for results.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve process capability, product conformity, yield, and manufacturing performance through effective process controls and proactive risk management.
* Lead targeted continuous improvement and change implementation across the two sites; standardize effective practices and verify that improvements are sustained.
* Ensure timely containment, disciplined root cause analysis, corrective/preventive action, and effectiveness verification for significant quality issues; deploy lessons learned across all two sites.
* Ensure practical, sustained application of SPC, MSA, FMEA, control plans, APQP, PPAP, 8D, A3, and DMAIC methodologies, as applicable to site processes and customer requirements.
* Serve as the quality escalation leader for the two Texas sites; communicate risk, containment status, recovery plans, and decisions needed, and escalate significant issues to Quality leadership.
* Partner with Customer Quality and Product Quality teams to resolve customer issues through timely, evidence-based investigations, effective corrective actions, and proactive communication.
* Develop site quality leaders and teams through coaching, clear expectations, technical capability building, and succession planning; identify staffing and resource needs across the two sites.
* Foster shared quality ownership across functions, reinforce accountability for commitments, and promote collaboration and continuous improvement across the two sites.
* Travel requirements will be a minimum of 25%, including regular presence across the two Texas sites.

**WHAT WE SEEK**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related field required.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing quality, including leadership responsibility for quality teams and manufacturing quality outcomes.
* 5+ years of quality management experience, with demonstrated ability to lead through site leaders or cross-functional teams; multi-site leadership experience preferred.
* Demonstrated success implementing quality systems and delivering sustained improvements in manufacturing quality, process capability, and cost of poor quality.
* Ability to coordinate priorities, standardize practices, and maintain effective leadership presence across two manufacturing sites in Texas.
* Experience supporting customer and supplier quality requirements, audit readiness, and compliance with applicable regulatory and industry requirements.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence site leaders, resolve competing priorities, and communicate risks and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Demonstrated experience coaching quality leaders, developing technical capability, and building team depth and succession readiness across sites.
* Demonstrated ability to lead practical change, establish clear ownership, and sustain common quality practices in partnership with Operations and Engineering.
* Strong problem-solving, data analysis, and business acumen, with practical application of quality tools to prioritize risk, improve manufacturing processes, and deliver measurable results.

**WHY WORK AT ENTEGRIS?**  
Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future.  
  
Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.

**WHAT WE OFFER**  
Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals.

* Compensation: The salary range for this position is $134,000- $196,500 per year. Final compensation will depend on the candidate's overall skills and qualifications for the role.
* Annual bonus eligibility
* Progressive paid time off policy that empowers you to take the time you need to recharge
* Generous 401(K) plan with an impressive employer match with no delayed vesting
* Excellent health, dental and vision insurance packages to fit your needs

protected_roles.description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talent team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels included, respected, empowered and recognised.

**What You Can Expect**
-----------------------

The Director, NPI Execution, M&A Integration & Supplier Transfers leads strategic execution across new product introduction, acquired-business integration, and supplier/manufacturing transfer initiatives. This senior leader is accountable for ensuring products, processes, supply chains, and teams transition successfully from development, acquisition, or incumbent suppliers into stable, compliant, scalable operations.  
The role requires strong business judgment, deep supply-base knowledge, technical fluency, and the ability to lead complex programs in a regulated medical-device environment. The Director partners closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Finance, Manufacturing Engineering, and leadership to deliver continuity of supply, cost competitiveness, product quality, and growth objectives.  
  
Reports to: Senior Director Procurement (Cost Center - M&A)  
Direct reports: Integration Program leaders, supplier-transfer leaders, NPI project managers, supplier development personnel

**How You'll Create Impact**
----------------------------

1. NPI Execution and Operational Readiness  

* Lead the end-to-end operational execution of New Product Introduction programs, from design-transfer planning through commercialization and sustained production.
* Establish integrated NPI execution plans & Ensure alignment between product development timelines and operational deliverables, including design transfer, process characterization, validation, supplier readiness, and product availability.
* Drive structured phase-gate governance with external suppliers , program reviews, escalation mechanisms, and executive decision-making for high-priority launches.

  
2. M&A Operations Integration  

* Serve as the Procurement lead for M&A integrations.
* Executes the integration for acquired companies for mitigation of supply-chain risk, supplier dependencies, tier-II management, partners with SQ team for quality-system maturity.
* Define and lead integration roadmaps for acquired businesses, including supplier onboarding, quality-system alignment, tier-II management and smooth transition to Contract manufacturing partner(s)
* Lead Procurement part of integration governance, ensuring milestones, decisions, risks, and accountabilities are visible and managed at the appropriate leadership level.

  
3. Supplier Transfer and Supply-Base Optimization  

* Lead complex supplier-transfer programs, including strategic sourcing transitions, supplier exits, dual-source strategies, vertical-integration initiatives, and manufacturing footprint changes.
* Develop transfer strategies that balance continuity of supply, quality, technical feasibility, regulatory requirements, cost, capacity, and timing.
* Ensure supplier transfers are executed in accordance with applicable quality-system requirements, change-control processes, validation requirements, and regulatory commitments.
* Direct supplier selection, qualification, technical transfer, process validation, first-article activities, production ramp-up, and supplier performance monitoring.

  
4. People Leadership and Organizational Capability  

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of program, technical, supply-chain, and supplier-management professionals.
* Set clear goals, priorities, performance expectations, and development plans for direct reports.
* Build succession capability and strengthen organizational depth in NPI execution, technical operations, supplier transfer, and integration management.
* Foster cross-functional collaboration among teams with potentially competing objectives, timelines, and priorities.

**What Makes You Stand Out**
----------------------------

Leadership  

* Builds high-performing teams and develops future leaders.
* Establishes clarity, accountability, and disciplined execution
* Leads through ambiguity, organizational change, and competing business priorities.

Business Acumen  

* Connects technical and operational decisions to financial, customer, and enterprise outcomes.
* Evaluates strategic tradeoffs with an enterprise-wide perspective.
* Identifies opportunities for value creation, risk reduction, and sustainable growth.

Technical and Procurement Expertise  

* Understands manufacturing processes, product industrialization, supplier capabilities, process controls, validation, and quality-system expectations.
* Demonstrates strong command of supply-base dynamics, supplier economics, sourcing strategy, and operational risk.
* Can challenge technical assumptions constructively and facilitate fact-based decisions.

Program Execution  

* Drives complex initiatives from strategy through implementation and stabilization.
* Uses effective governance, metrics, risk management, and escalation practices.
* Maintains focus on customer service, quality, compliance, delivery, and financial results.

Influence and Collaboration  

* Builds credibility with senior leaders, technical experts, plant leadership, suppliers, and all other stakeholders.
* Resolves conflict constructively and aligns diverse stakeholders behind common objectives.
* Communicates complex issues in a concise, actionable manner.

**Your Background**
-------------------

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, or a related technical discipline.
* Approximately 20 years of progressive experience in medical devices, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, or another highly regulated industry.
* Hands on experience & leadership experience in one or more of the following areas:
* New Product Introduction and product industrialization
* Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management
* Supplier Transfers or Manufacturing Transfers
* Mergers, Acquisitions, and Business Integration
* Supply Chain, Procurement, or Operations Program Management
* Proven people-management experience, including leading managers and technical professionals in a matrixed global environment.
* Strong knowledge of supplier qualification, supplier development, capacity planning, quality agreements, process validation, and manufacturing transfer principles.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate and manage supply-base risk, including sole-source exposure, capacity constraints, supplier quality issues, and business-continuity risks.
* Strong financial acumen, including business-case development, cost analysis, budget ownership, and value-capture management.
* Excellent executive communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and influencing skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Supply Chain, or a related discipline.
* Experience supporting medical-device product launches and design-transfer activities.
* Experience integrating acquired companies, product portfolios, manufacturing sites, or supplier networks.
* Familiarity with regulated quality systems and supplier-control expectations.
* Experience with lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, operational excellence, or structured problem-solving methodologies.
* Experience leading global suppliers and geographically distributed teams.
* Professional certifications in program management, supply chain, quality, or lean methodologies are desirable.

------------------------------

protected_roles.description:
Job ID

JR112695

**Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for** ***all*****.**

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

**Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.**

Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from virtual reality experiences to breakthroughs in neural networks possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing.

**Job Summary**

The Senior Director, Semiconductor Sourcing and NPI Procurement leads the global strategy, sourcing, and supplier ecosystem for wafer foundry services, IP and EDA services, discrete actives semiconductors, and 3rd party NAND flash controller categories as well as the New Product Introduction Procurement function. This role is accountable for delivering cost competitiveness, supply assurance, and long-term resilience across a complex semiconductor value chain.

Partnering closely with engineering, manufacturing, and business leaders, the role drives category strategies, supplier performance, and risk mitigation at category and product level while enabling Micron’s growth and innovation priorities. Success in this role requires deep semiconductor domain expertise, strong commercial acumen, and the ability to lead large, global teams to deliver enterprise-level outcomes.

**Main Responsibilities**

* Define and execute global procurement strategies for wafer foundry services, IP and EDA services, discrete actives semiconductors, and 3rd party NAND flash controller categories to support business growth and operational excellence
* Drive adherence to New Product Introduction metrics such as multi-sourcing, part reuse and golden part usage through stage gate reviews and collaboration with commodity category sourcing teams.
* Lead category management, ensuring cost competitiveness, supply continuity, and alignment with Micron’s strategic and financial objectives
* Build and manage strategic supplier partnerships, driving collaboration, performance accountability, and continuous improvement across the supplier ecosystem
* Ensure supply assurance through proactive capacity planning, demand-supply alignment, and risk mitigation strategies, including development of resilient global sourcing networks
* Drive end-to-end sourcing execution, including commercial negotiations, contract management, and supplier performance governance
* Lead cost optimization initiatives and negotiations to achieve best-in-class total cost of ownership
* Partner with cross-functional teams (engineering, manufacturing, supply chain) to support product, technology, and operational requirements
* Lead, develop, and scale a high-performing global procurement organization, including leading leaders and building long-term capability
* Establish KPIs and performance frameworks to drive operational excellence and continuous improvement across procurement and supplier performance
* Provide strategic leadership aligned to corporate priorities, ensuring clear line of sight from category execution to enterprise outcomes

**Other Responsibilities**

* Drive supplier diversity, sustainability, and responsible sourcing initiatives aligned with Micron’s commitments
* Strengthen procurement analytics, predictive capabilities, and digital transformation initiatives
* Represent procurement in executive-level forums and contribute to enterprise strategic planning
* Support crisis management and rapid response for supply disruptions or geopolitical risks
* Mentor emerging leaders and build succession pipelines within the procurement organization

* Integrate AI-enabled tools and predictive insights into procurement, sourcing, and supplier management to improve decision quality and efficiency
* Identify and scale AI-driven opportunities (e.g., demand forecasting, risk analytics, cost modeling) within procurement operations
* Foster a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement through responsible AI adoption

**Candidate Profile / Job Requirements**

**Minimum Required Qualifications / Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or equivalent practical experience
* 15+ years of experience across semiconductor manufacturing, procurement, or supplier management
* Proven experience operating at a global or enterprise leadership level, driving cross-functional business outcomes
* Track record in managing complex supplier ecosystems and outsourced manufacturing models

**Must Have Technical Skills**

* Deep understanding of wafer foundry landscape and ASIC development and manufacturing models (technical, operational, and commercial dimensions).
* Strong commercial acumen with experience negotiating complex, high-value agreements
* Expertise in category strategy, cost modeling, and total cost of ownership optimization
* Strong knowledge of global supply chain risks, capacity planning, and supplier performance management
* Familiarity with procurement analytics, digital tools, and data-driven decision-making

**Must Have Soft Skills**

* Strong enterprise leadership capability, including leading leaders and influencing across global organizations
* Strategic thinking with the ability to translate vision into execution
* Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills across executive and operational levels
* High resilience and decision-making capability in complex, ambiguous environments
* Ability to build and lead high-performing, scalable teams

**AI Requirements**

* Demonstrates strong digital fluency and ability to leverage AI-enabled tools in procurement, analytics, and decision-making
* Applies AI responsibly in alignment with organizational standards and governance

**Highly Desirable / Preferred**

* Experience sourcing discrete active semiconductor components used in SSD and Memory Modules
* Experience managing IP and EDA suppliers
* Exposure to global manufacturing networks
* Experience leading procurement transformation or digital initiatives
* Strong understanding of semiconductor market dynamics and macro trends

**Embody Micron’s Core Values**

* People – Respect, develop, and empower others
* Innovation – Drive continuous improvement and breakthrough thinking
* Tenacity – Demonstrate grit and resilience
* Collaboration – Build trust across global teams and partners
* Customer Focus – Deliver value and enable business success

$199,000.00 - $349,000.00 a year
